Chapter 18

The Birthday Cake

Happy birthday, Mia. Sorry about the cake.

Read this aloud

There are balloons on the gate of Number 5 and music inside. Dad carries a cake in from the car and straight through to the kitchen — chocolate, three layers, under a plastic cover — and the guests are still arriving. In the dining room, a grey parrot shouts “PARTY!” at nobody. Aunt Rosalind, who notices everything, is already sitting in the best chair.

At a glance

House Hard · Patience 6 · The prize birthday cake (Medium, portions: 2 per cat; hauling it is Tricky) · Gone at the start of round 9 · Den Downstairs loo

Who lives here Dad, Aunt Rosalind, Mia, Leo, Captain the parrot

Three cats Patience 7, gone at the start of round 10, Lights Out at the end of round 12, 3 Cattitude each · Five cats Patience 5, gone at the start of round 10, Lights Out at the end of round 12

A birthday party: the house is full of people. Dad is in the kitchen with the cake, Aunt Rosalind holds court in the dining room, and Mia and her brother Leo run everywhere. The patio door is open for the guests. At the start of round 5 the cake goes to the dining-room table for the candles, and it will be cut and served at the start of round 8.

How it plays

  • There are four humans and a parrot. You can’t distract them all; work out who will be where.
  • Aunt Rosalind has Attention 2: Sneaky and Sweet are hard under her nose.
  • Two kids double every Cuddle step — and once Cuddle is the fuller meter, any cat’s Flop in front of a kid is 4 Cuddle steps. The Muscle gets scooped here too.
  • The cake wobbles: hauling it is Tricky. Carrying it out whole would be a Clean Getaway, but it takes two shaky hauls past a dining room full of people — eating it is the surer plan.
  • Eating half the cake is a Messy Getaway — and at this house that’s a good night.

The Prize Clock

WhenThe prize
Start of round 1Dad puts it in the kitchen and stays there this round. Step 1: climb up to it (a Climber’s Knack) (Sneaky or Savage, Tricky); then step 2: get the wrapping off (a Curious cat’s Knack) (Streetwise or Savage, Tricky).
Start of round 5Dad puts it in the dining room and stays there this round. Step 1: climb up to it (a Climber’s Knack) (Sneaky or Savage, Tricky).
Start of round 9Gone — unless the gang has got it out or a cat is holding it.
End of round 11Lights Out: any cat still inside is pinched.

The front door keeps opening for guests, so it works in rounds 1 and 2 (one cat each round); the guests count as a human with Attention 0 who fills no meter, though a Scrape or Flop at the door is still a noise in the hall. The patio door is open and needs no roll — but it opens into the dining room, where Aunt Rosalind and Captain are.

The getaway

  1. The party gate, through the guests’ legs — Sweet; or Sneaky or Savage, Tricky.
  2. Next door’s bouncy castle — Savage or Sneaky, Tricky. The Party Crashers hang about here, and nick any loot that’s dropped.
  3. The high back fence — Savage, Tricky; or Sneaky, Hard.
  4. The ring road — Streetwise or Savage, Tricky.

Then the hideout. The loot is its portions — whatever wasn’t eaten inside.

Cred (Chapter 9): the catnip stash is a catnip toy, wrapped as a present for Gran’s cat (utility room). The Party Crashers have tagged the hall.
